entries.addVersion: Add a version in another language
entries.newVersionHint: This entry has no {lang} version yet. Fill the form to add one — it is optional, the other languages are untouched.
redirects.intro: A redirect sends /path to an external address you explicitly allow. Nothing else can be redirected to: there is no open redirect.
redirects.targetHelp: https://… address to send visitors to.
redirects.orEntryHelp: The redirect will always use that entry's current link.
redirects.permanent: Permanent (301/308) — leave unchecked if the target may change
redirects.error.reserved: This path is reserved or used by a collection.
redirects.error.exists: This path already has a redirect.
home.intro: The home page has no content of its own: it is an assembly of sections offered by your module instances. Pick, order and configure them.
navigation.intro: Collections shown in the menu (blog, sponsors…) appear automatically first. Here, build the rest: your pages and your links, in any order you like.
navigation.label: Label
navigation.error.label: Give each link a label in at least one language.
settings.languagesHelp: The default language has no URL prefix; the others live under /en, /fr… Content is never forced to exist in every language.
settings.adminLocaleHelp: Each user can override it in their account.
settings.autoDetect: Detect the visitor's language on first visit
settings.autoDetectHelp: Based on the browser language, only on the home page.
settings.appearanceHelp: Text and surface colors are derived automatically so they stay readable.
modules.intro: Everything on the site is a module: blogs, social links, promo codes, pages, the home banner, RSS, the contact form… Each module can have several instances — two blogs, two lists of social links (one per channel) — each with its own settings, content, address and admin entry.
modules.broken: This module cannot be loaded (see server logs).
modules.uninstallConfirm: Uninstall this module and delete its data and settings?
modules.install: Install a module from a git repository
modules.warning: A module is code that runs on your server with full access to your site. Only install modules from authors you trust, and read the code first. A module is installed disabled; nothing runs until you enable it.
modules.repoHelp: https://host/owner/repo — add #tag or #branch to pin a version.
modules.disabledNotice: This module is disabled: its instances do not appear on the site. Enable it from the modules list.
modules.error.host: This host is not allowed (see MODULES_ALLOWED_HOSTS).
modules.error.clone: The repository could not be downloaded.
modules.error.nomanifest: No valid module.json at the root of the repository.
modules.error.nomain: The file declared in "main" does not exist.
modules.error.exists: A module with this id is already installed.
modules.error.builtin: This id is reserved by a built-in module.
modules.error.load: The module could not be loaded.

setup.account.title: Last step, {name}: your access
setup.account.name: Your name
setup.account.passwordHelp: At least 10 characters. A sentence you'll remember is perfect.
setup.account.tokenHelp: The code you were given with your server: it stops a stranger from claiming a brand-new site.
setup.error.password: The password needs at least 10 characters.
instances.add: Add an instance (new blog, new list…)
instances.basePathHelp: /blog → https://site/blog. Empty = at the site root (/my-page).
instances.customFieldsHelp: One per line: key | label | type (text, url, number, boolean).
instances.fallback: Fall back to the default language
instances.fallbackHelp: Show the default-language version when an entry is not translated.
instances.goLinksHelp: Short redirect to the entry's link.
instances.deleteWarning: Deleting an instance also deletes its entries, settings and stored data.
instances.error.path: The URL segment may only contain lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
instances.error.pathUsed: Another instance already uses this URL segment.
instances.error.redirectClash: A redirect already uses this path.
instances.error.name: The name in the default language is required.
instances.error.single: This module allows a single instance.
home.optionsHint: After saving, the options of each section (for example how many entries) appear on its row.
field.tagsHelp: Comma-separated. Other modules (overlays…) can filter entries by tag.
instances.exposed: Offer its entries to other modules
instances.exposedHelp: Overlays and other modules can use this instance's published entries (topic core.entry). They only see what is public.
sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: This module digests information offered by others. Choose which instances feed it; all checked means every source, including ones you add later.
sources.none: No instance offers this kind of information yet.
sources.tags: Only entries with one of these tags
mode.help: Simple mode shows what most people need. Advanced mode adds technical settings (URLs, fields, sources, installation from git…). Nothing you set in one mode is lost in the other.
editor.heading: Heading
redirects.introSimple: A shortcut is a short address on your site that sends visitors somewhere else. For example, "{site}/twitch" can lead to your Twitch channel: easy to say out loud, to put in a bio or under a video, and if your link ever changes you only update it here.
modules.introSimple: This is what your site does. Switch each feature on or off, and adjust it in one click.
dashboard.shortcutsHelp: Short addresses like /twitch that lead to your links.
dashboard.addFeatureHelp: A second blog, a contact form, an overlay for your stream…
dashboard.viewSiteHelp: Open it the way visitors see it.
mcp.title: API & MCP
mcp.intro: MCP lets an AI assistant (Claude, for example) work on your site through the actions that your modules declare: read your content, draft articles, update your partnership pipeline. Nobody can use it without a token, and each token only gets the actions you grant.
mcp.off: MCP is disabled — nobody can use it, tokens included.
mcp.safety: Safety rules that cannot be changed: a read-only token never writes; irreversible actions are never on by default; every write is recorded in the audit log; the content editor only lets an assistant create or edit drafts.
mcp.scopeHelp: The ceiling of the token. “Read & write” allows write actions to be granted; you still choose them one by one afterwards.
mcp.tokenCreated: Copy this token now, it will not be shown again:
mcp.toolsHelp: Collected from every active module. Modules and instances can opt out (advanced settings of the instance).
instances.mcp: Offer its actions to the MCP API
instances.mcpHelp: Assistants connected through MCP can use this instance's actions (drafts, internal files…).
mcp.accessIntro: Choose, action by action, what this token may do. Changes apply immediately — no need to create a new token. Each module decides which of its actions are on by default; the others stay off until you turn them on here.
mcp.readCeiling: This is a read-only token: actions that write stay locked, whatever is checked. Create a read & write token to allow them.
mcp.resetAll: Reset every action of this token to the module defaults
mcp.instanceOptedOut: This instance has withdrawn its actions from MCP (advanced settings of the instance): nothing here can be used.
mcp.confirmDestructive: “{action}” is irreversible (it deletes data). Allow this token to do it?
settings.aboutHelp: Markdown. Shown wherever the site presents itself, for example in a press kit.
brand.role.accentFg: Text placed on the accent color
instances.nicknameAdminHelp: Tells your {module} instances apart in the admin (not shown on the site). The site's own name for it is set below.
instances.nicknameHelp: Short and recognizable: it is how you will find it in the menus. Only used to tell them apart.
instances.error.nickname.empty: Give a nickname so you can tell them apart.
instances.error.nickname.long: This nickname is too long (40 characters maximum).
instances.error.nickname.taken: Another one already has this nickname.
settings.mailHelp: The site's outgoing mail server (SMTP). Modules use it to notify you; they never see the password.
settings.mailPassHelp: Leave empty to keep the current one. It is never shown again.
settings.mailTest: Send a test email to my address
settings.mailStatusOff: No email server: modules cannot send messages.
settings.mailTestFail: Sending failed. Check the server, port and password.
settings.mailTestBody: If you can read this, sending email works.
instances.followThemeHelp: The color adapts when you change the theme in Settings.
home.sizeHelp: The home page is fluid: blocks flow onto the next line depending on space, and stack on a small screen. “Alone on its row” puts a block on its own, centered. The size only says how much room a block likes to take; the default is the feature's recommendation.
home.isolatedHelp: Alone on its own line, centered, with a line break before and after; the following pieces then flow on normally.
updates.unreachable: The repository could not be reached.
updates.confirm: Before updating: the database is backed up, then the new (already compiled) version is downloaded, verified and installed; if anything fails, the previous version is restored automatically. The site is unavailable for a moment while it restarts.
updates.started: Update to {version} started. This page refreshes by itself.
updates.majorWarning: Major version: it may change how the site works. Read its release notes before installing; it is never installed automatically.
updates.restartNeeded: The server must be restarted for the change to take effect (no restart command is configured).
updates.autoHelp: Off by default. When on, the site checks every 6 hours and installs fixes and new features by itself (never a major change), with a backup and automatic rollback on failure.
updates.mode.docker: This site runs in a container: update it by replacing the image (rebuild and restart the container), not from the admin.
updates.mode.manual: This site wasn't installed from a release archive: updating from the admin isn't available. See the installation docs.
updates.restart.command: After installation, the server is restarted by the command you configured.
updates.restart.supervised: After installation, the server stops and its supervisor (systemd, pm2, Docker…) restarts it.
updates.restart.manual: No restart command is configured: after installation, restart the server by hand.
updates.error.not-newer: That version is not newer than the installed one.
updates.error.unsupported: This installation cannot update from the admin.
catalogue.intro: Modules verified for this framework: shipped with it, or published in recognized repositories. You can also install a personal, unverified repository.
catalogue.examples: Examples (to learn how to build a module)
catalogue.customWarning: A module is code that runs on your server with the same rights as the site. A personal repository is verified by nobody: only install code whose author you know, and read it. It is installed disabled; you enable it afterwards.
catalogue.trust: I understand this code is not verified and will run on my server.
catalogue.trustRequired: Tick the box to confirm you understand the risk.
modules.error.idmismatch: This repository does not provide the announced module.
modules.error.incompatible: This module is not compatible with this framework version.
backup.intro: Your data (content, settings, users, module data, images) in a single encrypted file, readable later even without this framework.
backup.createHelp: Choose a password: it encrypts the file and is stored nowhere.
backup.passwordWarning: At least {n} characters. Without this password the backup cannot be recovered: there is no way to retrieve it. Write it down elsewhere.
backup.readWithout: How to read a backup without the framework?
backup.readWithoutHelp: With OpenSSL then tar (on Linux and macOS, installable on Windows). The resulting folder has a README.txt explaining the rest and a "readable" folder with your data as Markdown, JSON and CSV:
backup.restoreHelp: Modules are reinstalled from the catalog. A personal module (unverified repository) is only reinstalled if you confirm it, one by one.
backup.done: Restore complete. Sign in again with an account from the backup.
backup.replaceWarning: Restoring REPLACES the site's current data with the backup's. A copy of the current database is kept in data/backups/.
backup.confirmReplace: Replace all current data with the backup's?
backup.trustCustom: Reinstall this unverified personal module from:
backup.status.catalogue: will be reinstalled from the catalog
backup.status.unavailable: not found (its data is kept, but the module must be reinstalled by hand)
backup.error.not-a-backup: This file is not a backup of this framework.
backup.error.corrupt: The file is corrupted or incomplete.
backup.error.tampered: The backup was modified or is incomplete: refused.
backup.error.newer-schema: This backup comes from a newer database version: update the framework first.
backup.error.newer-format: This backup comes from a newer framework version: update it first.
backup.error.no-owner: This backup has no owner: refused so you are not locked out.
backup.error.expired: The preview expired (30 minutes): start again.
backup.error.failed: The restore failed; nothing was changed.
setup.restore.link: I already have a backup: restore it instead of creating a new site
setup.restore.title: Restore a backup
setup.restore.help: Get your site back as it was: content, settings, users, modules (reinstalled from the catalog) and images. Choose your backup file and the password you picked when creating it.
backup.error.already-configured: This site is already configured: sign in to the admin to restore.

catalogue.source.cache: Framework repository unreachable: last list received on {date}.
catalogue.source.snapshot: List shipped with this framework version (the repository could not be reached or is not configured).
modules.updateAvailableTo: An update of {module} is available: {version}. Your data and settings are kept.
modules.updateMajor: Major change: the module may work differently. Read its release notes before installing. If the new version is invalid, the previous one is restored automatically.
modules.error.uptodate: This module is already up to date.
modules.error.pinned: This module is pinned to a specific commit: it does not update.
migration.failed: Updating this instance's data failed: it was put back to its previous state and set aside (it does not run on half-converted data). A copy of the database is in data/backups/. Fix or update the module, then retry.
migration.newer: This instance's data is newer than the installed module's code (backup restored into an older module?). Update the module, then retry.
modules.error.migration: Module updated, but the data migration of at least one instance failed: it was put back to its previous state and set aside. Open it to retry.
tasks.title: Scheduled tasks
settings.blockAiBotsHelp: robots.txt disallows AI scraping bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot…). No search engine is blocked.
audit.intro: Who did what, and when (sign-ins, settings, modules, backups…). Message contents are never logged.
modules.error.requires: This module needs: {services}. No active module offers it, and none ships with the framework: install one (catalog) and try again.
modules.error.requiredBy: Not possible: these active modules depend on it ({modules}). Disable them first.
services.title: Services offered by several modules
services.intro: Several modules offer the same service. The master receives the calls and answers; replicas also receive what is written (from now on: data already received is not copied).
services.pending: To be chosen: until then, the first provider is the master, with no replica.
services.notice: This module offers a service that other modules already offer: choose which one is the master.
services.hint: Drag the arrow from the service dot to a provider (or click one).
catalogue.previewFailed: Could not read this repository (address refused, private repository or unreachable). Nothing was installed.
instances.displayNameHelp: The name you and your visitors will see for this feature.

settings.moreLanguages: Offer the site in other languages
instances.deleteWarning.simple: This removes the feature from your site, along with what it contains. There is no undo.
home.intro.simple: Build your home page like a set of bricks: add blocks, put them in order with the arrows, choose their size.
home.empty: Your home page is empty for now. Add a first block!
home.pick: What do you want to show?
setup.welcome.title: Welcome 👋
setup.welcome.text: I'll help you set up your site in a few minutes. First, let's get to know each other.
setup.welcome.name: What's your name?
setup.welcome.nameHelp: Your first name is enough: that's how your dashboard will talk to you.
setup.account.help: Your email and password will let you sign back in to your dashboard.
dashboard.welcome: Your site is live, {name}! Here's where to start: write a first post, pick your colors, or go and see the result.
updates.rcWarning: ⚠️ This version is a release candidate: it hasn't finished being tested and may contain defects. At your own risk — take a real backup first (Backup page).
updates.channelHelp: By default the site only offers stable versions. Release candidates are upcoming versions published ahead of release so they can be tested. Going back to the stable channel doesn't downgrade you: you stay on your version until a newer stable one is out.
updates.channelRisk: I understand this is at my own risk
updates.channelRiskHelp: A release candidate is never installed automatically, even when automatic updates are on.
settings.glowHelp: Large soft colour spots taken from your accent colour, behind the content. Best on a dark background.
settings.glow.tuningHelp: Used when "Custom" is chosen above. Out-of-range values are brought back to the nearest limit.
settings.glow.sizeHelp: 30 to 120. A large spot blends into the background.
settings.glow.varianceHelp: 0: all alike. 100: from very small to very large.
settings.glow.hueHelp: 0: all in the accent colour. 180: each spot may take any hue around the accent (±°).
settings.glow.intensityHelp: Maximum opacity of a spot's core, 5 to 50.
settings.glow.seedHelp: 1 to 9999. Changes the random positions, sizes and hues; the same value always gives the same layout.
settings.bgHelp: A backdrop behind the content, built from your colours. It adds to the glow above.
settings.bgCustomHelp: Used when "Custom" is chosen. A list of layers (gradient, spots, dots, grid, image), 6 at most: see docs/BACKGROUND.md. Nothing is saved if the description is invalid.
navigation.empty: Nothing here yet: add a page or a link.
navigation.pickPage: Which page do you want in the menu?
navigation.noMorePages: All your pages are already in the menu.
settings.glow.colorHelp: Used when the box above is unchecked. The "hue shift" applies starting from this colour.
settings.bgSvgHelp: Paste the code of an SVG drawing (exported from Inkscape, Figma, Illustrator…): gradients, dot patterns, silhouettes, motifs. It needs a viewBox. Colours can follow the theme: write {accent}, {bg}, {fg}… instead of a colour code. No scripts, text or embedded images: see docs/BACKGROUND.md.
settings.bgSvgAlignHelp: When the window doesn't have the drawing's proportions, the drawing is cropped: choose which side stays visible.
settings.faviconHelp: A square image (png, jpg, webp or gif; 64 × 64 px or larger). Without an image, the site builds an icon from its colours.
instances.sortHelp: Newest first by default. A "featured" entry always comes first.
sort.title: By title (A → Z)
settings.statsHelp: Daily counters shown on the dashboard: no IP address, cookie or identifier is ever kept. Visitors who refuse tracking (Do Not Track) are not counted.
dashboard.visitsPrivacy: Anonymous counting: no personal data is kept.
redirects.examples: Examples: /twitch → your channel, /shop → your online shop, /donate → your support page.
redirects.howTo: How: pick a short word (the "path"), then paste the full destination address, which starts with https://.
settings.logosHelp: Upload what you have: nothing is required, the site does its best with the images it receives.
settings.logoWideHelp: Symbol and name side by side. Shown at the top of the site instead of the written name.
settings.logoSquareHelp: The symbol alone. Used small (phone, badges) and in place of the horizontal logo when it is missing.
settings.logoShareHelp: Shown when the site is shared (social networks, messengers). Ideal: 1200 × 630 px. Without one, the site uses your icon.
settings.logosDarkHelp: If your site has a dark background and your logo is dark, upload a light version here. The site picks the right one from the background color.
navigation.groupEmpty: This menu is empty: add pages or links to it (an empty menu is not saved).
settings.headerHelp: Choose the layout of the top of your pages. The logo, menu, languages and the elements below place themselves.
settings.header.classicHelp: Logo on the left, menu on the right.
settings.header.twoRowsHelp: Logo and button on top, menu below.
settings.header.centeredHelp: Logo in the middle, menu centered below.
settings.header.minimalHelp: Logo and a "Menu" button: discreet, on large screens too.
settings.header.socialsHelp: Uses the links of your social network lists (all of them): nothing to retype.
settings.header.label: Text
settings.header.linksHelp: A link or button only appears when both its text and address are filled. The address is a site page (/contact), an https://… link or mailto:…
settings.privacyHelp: What the site measures and what it lets robots do.
settings.privacyCookies: Unless a visitor turns on the "news" button, the site sets no tracking cookie: only the chosen language.
site.newsHelp: Remembers the date of your last visit in your browser to flag what is new. A second click erases everything.
settings.newsToggle: Let visitors choose to be notified of news
settings.newsToggleHelp: Adds a "Notify me of news" button to the header. The menu's news dots only appear for visitors who turned it on: nothing is stored for the others, so no cookie banner is needed.
settings.privacyLaw: Statistics store nothing in the browser and keep no personal data (no banner needed). Remember to say so on your site's privacy page: see docs/PRIVACY.md.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page describes what the site "{name}" records about you. It is generated automatically from how the site really works.
privacy.whoContact: The site "{name}" is run by its owner. For any question about your data, write to {email}.
privacy.whoNoContact: The site "{name}" is run by its owner. For any question about your data, use the contact details given on the site.
privacy.cookies: Cookies and storage in your browser
privacy.cookies.locale: **Language**: the site remembers the language you choose (cookie "curiosa_locale", 1 year). It is needed to show you the site in the right language.
privacy.cookies.news: **News**: only if you turn on the "Notify me of news" button yourself, the site remembers in your browser the date of your last visit to flag what is new (cookies "curiosa_news", "curiosa_seen" and "curiosa_since", up to 1 year). A second click on the button erases everything.
privacy.cookies.none: The site sets no advertising or tracking cookie and uses no third-party measurement service.
privacy.stats.on: The site counts its visits anonymously: page views, most read pages and where visitors come from, as daily counters. Nothing is stored in your browser and your IP address is never recorded; to count a visitor only once a day, the server derives a single-use fingerprint from it, deleted the next day, which cannot recognise you from one day to the next. Visitors who send "Do Not Track" or "Global Privacy Control" are not counted.
privacy.stats.off: The site does not count its visits.
privacy.features: Data collected by the site's features
privacy.rights.text: You can ask for access to the data about you, for its correction or erasure, object to its processing, or lodge a complaint with the competent data protection authority.
settings.privacyPageHelp: This page is created by the site's core and stays shown at the bottom of every page: the mandatory text (cookies, statistics, your features' data, visitors' rights) is generated from what the site really does and cannot be removed. You can only add your own information to it.
settings.privacyExtraHelp: Simple Markdown. Shown after the mandatory text: data controller, retention period, how to exercise rights…
